purpose: Convert observed historical update/recovery transaction gaps into deterministic H1/H2/H3 and acceptance regression cases without executing destructive operations on a real system.

oracles.historical_mechanism: Preflight checks repo/.git and lock state but does not reject/snapshot tracked uncommitted changes; rollback executes git reset --hard <backup_sha>.
oracles.adversarial_setup: Create a tracked local edit, then force a post-pull rollback-triggering failure.
oracles.historical_risk: The local edit can be destroyed by rollback even though it is outside the update payload.
oracles.required_current_behavior: Fail closed on dirty authoritative state or snapshot/reify it as a separately recoverable version before update; rollback must not silently erase unrelated local state.

oracles.historical_mechanism: A lock older than 600 seconds is unlinked based only on mtime; stored PID is not checked for liveness/ownership.
oracles.adversarial_setup: Keep an update legitimately active longer than 600 seconds and start a second updater.
oracles.historical_risk: Second updater may delete the first updater's lock and overlap a live transaction.
oracles.required_current_behavior: Lease/lock identity must bind owner process identity plus heartbeat/epoch; stale reclamation requires proof of liveness loss or CAS-safe lease expiry.

oracles.historical_mechanism: Failed affected-service stops are warnings; step_stop_services() still returns True and the pull proceeds.
oracles.adversarial_setup: Make one stateful affected service refuse/timeout during stop.
oracles.historical_risk: Code/data may be mutated while a writer remains live; quiescence is asserted without being achieved.
oracles.required_current_behavior: A required quiescence barrier must be machine-verifiable and fail closed before any incompatible mutation.

oracles.historical_mechanism: pip install -r requirements.txt mutates the environment before later rollback-capable steps; rollback only performs git reset --hard and restarts services.
oracles.adversarial_setup: Change a dependency version, let pip sync succeed, then force a later rollback-triggering failure.
oracles.historical_risk: Source returns to old SHA while dependency environment remains at the new version, yielding a mixed-state rollback.
oracles.required_current_behavior: Update transaction identity must include source, dependency/runtime package set, config/service definitions, schema/data compatibility and model artifacts; rollback restores or switches the whole version set atomically.

oracles.historical_mechanism: Service start failures are warnings; step_start_services() always returns True.
oracles.adversarial_setup: Make one previously stopped required service fail to start after update.
oracles.historical_risk: The pipeline can proceed to completion despite a required service remaining down.
oracles.required_current_behavior: Required-service start is an acceptance gate; failure must trigger rollback/recovery or explicit degraded-state abort, never a success receipt.

oracles.historical_mechanism: step_health_check() records all_ok=False but always reports done and returns True; the main run also ignores its result and prints UPDATE COMPLETE.
oracles.adversarial_setup: Keep a required service inactive or make its health/inference endpoint fail after update.
oracles.historical_risk: Operationally unhealthy state is labeled successful deployment.
oracles.required_current_behavior: Health/inference/semantic readiness receipts are commit gates. A known failed required check cannot coexist with SUCCESS.

oracles.historical_mechanism: After rollback-gated steps finish, overlay environment code can rewrite ~/.config/systemd/user/frank-overlay.service, reload systemd and restart the overlay; these mutations are not covered by the saved git SHA rollback boundary.
oracles.adversarial_setup: Force overlay service-file repair, then fail a later model/readiness condition.
oracles.historical_risk: Successful-source rollback semantics do not cover post-transaction machine configuration mutations.
oracles.required_current_behavior: External machine/config effects require explicit effect receipts plus inverse/rollback semantics or immutable version switching.

oracles.historical_mechanism: Database recovery warns on failed service stops, then continues backup/wipe/copy; only llama-server is additionally pkilled.
oracles.adversarial_setup: Make one DB-writing service resist stop while recovery proceeds.
oracles.historical_risk: Backup/wipe can race a live writer, invalidating both backup consistency and destructive replacement safety.
oracles.required_current_behavior: All authoritative writers must prove quiescence/lease relinquishment before destructive recovery mutation.

oracles.historical_mechanism: Recovery copies reference DB files and restarts services but performs no post-copy SQLite integrity/schema/version checks and returns Recovery complete even if one or more service starts fail.
oracles.adversarial_setup: Provide a syntactically copied but incompatible/corrupt reference DB or force one service start failure.
oracles.historical_risk: A destructive recovery can end in an invalid data/runtime state while reporting success.
oracles.required_current_behavior: Recovery acceptance requires artifact hash/version identity, DB integrity+schema compatibility, required-service startup and semantic smoke/readiness checks before commit.

epistemic_boundary: These are code-derived historical failure oracles. They establish reachable fail-open/mixed-state paths in the reference logic; they are not claims that each failure occurred in production.
